forecaster_note: Mon: small little windswells, a couple of waist-high waves on the better banks; best at dawn on the lower tide, light winds clean until the high tide mark. NE winds add chop to the open beaches in the arvo. Tue: southerly change from Tasman troughs, S winds ramp up mid-morning — surf early for small clean waist high; lumpy chest high late arvo. Wed: intense southerly gusts and a spike of short-period S swell — S exposures well overhead to 2x mess, only waist-high sets at sheltered Sth corners. Thu: S swell in the well overhead range on S exposures, chance of a SW window at dawn. — Surfline forecaster, Mon 12 Oct

days.label: Today
days.note: Small clean windswell (E/SSE/NE mix, ~84 kJ, short period). Fair at Long Reef & Curl Curl, poor–fair at Dee Why & Manly. Light W offshore dawn — go 6–9am on the low-to-mid tide before the NE chop arvo. A mush-burger groveller day.
days.surfline_text: Small little windswells offer a couple waist high waves on the better banks and we'll see the best conditions at dawn with that lower tide. Worth bringing a lengthy voluminous board, light winds should keep it clean up until the high tide mark.  Into the afternoon NE winds add chop to the open beaches. Tuck into the Nth corners if your chasing that arvo low.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Small and clean early, then a southerly change ramps up from mid-morning. Surf at dawn for waist high; S winds trash the exposed breaks by noon, lumpy chest-high late arvo. Sth corners for a low-tide session.
days.surfline_text: Some troughy activity in the Tasman is set to whip up southerly winds. They're looking to ramp up around mid-morning so get out there early for something small and clean - around waist high.  The S winds will make a mess of the Sth exposed breaks by noon/mid arvo and we'll start to see lumpy chest high conditions emerge through the late arvo. Protected Sth corners will be go for a small low tide session.
